request: What impact did passing Obamacare have on the federal budget?

reply.reply: The best verified CRS evidence describes projections, not what ultimately happened: CBO and JCT projected that ACA implementation would reduce federal deficits by $210 billion over FY2012–FY2021 (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). The same report estimated net costs of $1,083 billion for insurance coverage expansion over that period, reflecting that this component alone had substantial costs; the projected overall deficit reduction included the law’s offsets and revenues (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). These are projections cited in a 2012 CRS report, not realized budget results or the original estimate made at passage. [See the brief](output/briefs/case-20261025-145338-812f.html).
reply.reasoning: Verified findings show a February 2011 CBO/JCT baseline projection and separate projected coverage-expansion net costs. The sources reviewed are dated 2012 and do not establish realized fiscal outcomes.
